questions.q: What is a global forecasting model?
options: A model for one big series
A model trained on many series together
why: That is a local model for one series.
Correct: windows of all series are pooled.
Global refers to the number of series, not to events.

questions.q: Why does a global model need per-series scaling?
options: So that large series do not dominate the training loss
Because models cannot read big numbers
why: Correct: raw errors of big series would outweigh the small ones.
Scaling does not slow the model.
Models can read them, but the fit is unbalanced.

questions.q: 200 series, each 60 points. Window 5, horizon 1. How many rows in the pooled table?
Which statement about series id as a feature is true?
options: It lets the model learn series-specific behaviour
It must always be one-hot encoded
It is not useful in global models
why: Correct: the model can separate series that behave differently.
With thousands of ids, use a categorical feature or embedding instead.
It is a standard feature in global models.

questions.q: Select all situations where a global model is a good first choice.
options: Many new items with short history
One very long, unique series with no related series
why: Yes. Pooling helps with many related series.
Yes. They borrow strength from older series.
No. A local model is a natural choice here.
Yes. The shared effects are learned from all series.

questions.q: A global model has a good average error, but the 20 largest products have a bad error. What do you do?
options: Ignore it, the average is good
Check error by segment, add features or train a separate model for the large products
Remove the large products from the test
why: The large products may carry most of the revenue.
Correct: segment-level errors guide a hybrid solution.
Removing hard cases is not fair.
